result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_edge_btwns()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using Edge Betweenness (Girvan-Newman) algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20398-L20506){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_edge_btwns( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge-betweenness communities](/assets/graphs/cmty-edge-btwns.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the bridge C to D, drawn dashed because every path between the clusters crosses it, so it has the highest betweenness and is the first edge Girvan-Newman cuts. The remaining pieces are the communities: 0 is A, B, C and 1 is D, E, F, G." width="100%"} Iteratively removes edges with highest betweenness centrality to reveal community structure. Uses Brandes' algorithm for efficient betweenness calculation. More accurate than Fast Greedy but significantly slower (`O(m²n)` complexity). Shares its implementation with `cmty_girvan_newman()`, so the two always return the same partition: ties for the highest betweenness go to the edge with the smallest endpoint IDs, and communities are numbered by their smallest node ID. Best for small to medium graphs (< 5K nodes) with hierarchical community structure and clear "bridge" edges between communities. When accuracy is more important than speed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_edge_btwns`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed, contiguous). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed (requires undirected graph). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The Girvan-Newman procedure (2002) treats community boundaries as bottlenecks that carry disproportionate edge betweenness: any shortest path connecting two communities must cross one of a few *bridge* edges, so those edges rack up high betweenness scores. The algorithm computes edge betweenness with Brandes' algorithm, removes the current maximum, and repeats, keeping whichever intermediate partition attains the highest modularity. Because betweenness has to be recomputed after every removal, the total cost is $O(m^2 n)$: fine for a few thousand nodes, punishing beyond ten thousand. `cmty_fast_greedy()` and `cmty_louvain()` scale much better, so reach for edge-betweenness when you want the divisive-hierarchical interpretation or when the graph is small enough that the extra cost buys real accuracy. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The bridge edge "C"-"D" has the highest betweenness of any edge here, since every path between the two triangles must cross it -- so it's the first edge removed, splitting the graph into its two natural communities: ::: {#c9484184 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), # Triangle 1 ("C", "D"), # Bridge edge ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) # Triangle 2 ) communities = graph.cmty_edge_btwns(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): cid for nid, cid in communities.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'C': 0, 'A': 0, 'E': 1, 'F': 1, 'D': 1, 'B': 0} ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute and chaining into `colorize_node_attrs()` visualizes the communities directly: ::: {#54a66fd8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), # Triangle 1 ("C", "D"), # Bridge edge ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) # Triangle 2 ) ( graph .cmty_edge_btwns(attr_name="community") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="Pastel1") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 6 Number of edges : 7 Directed : False Density : 0.47 Average degree (min, max) : 2.33 (2, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations: - cmty_edge_btwns() -> attr: 'community' (6 of 6 nodes) Node aesthetics: - color <- community via colorize (palette: "Pastel1") (values: #b3cde3, #fbb4ae, 6 of 6 nodes) ``` ::: :::
